identity.name: SRG HOUSING FINANCE L
identity.industry: Financial Services — Affordable Housing Finance (rural/semi-urban, self-employed segment)

summary.oneLiner:
First housing finance company of Rajasthan; small-ticket secured lending to rural/semi-urban self-employed
borrowers. FY26 crossed the INR 1,000 crore AUM milestone (INR 1,042 cr, +37% YoY) with a credit-rating upgrade
to Acuité A- Stable, opening up bank and equity funding channels; management now guides an aggressive
southward geographic expansion (Tamil Nadu, Telangana) and a long-term ambition of INR 10,000–20,000 cr AUM.

one-line thesis:
First housing finance company of Rajasthan; small-ticket secured lending to rural/semi-urban self-employed
borrowers. FY26 crossed the INR 1,000 crore AUM milestone (INR 1,042 cr, +37% YoY) with a credit-rating upgrade
to Acuité A- Stable, opening up bank and equity funding channels; management now guides an aggressive
southward geographic expansion (Tamil Nadu, Telangana) and a long-term ambition of INR 10,000–20,000 cr AUM.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Net interest income | ~INR 28 cr (Q4) | +33% | FY26 NII: INR 98.26 cr, +31% YoY |
| NIM | 11.28% (Q4) | — | FY26 NIM: 10.91% |
| PAT (rptd) | ~INR 9 cr (Q4) | +50% | FY26 PAT: INR 32.49 cr, +33% YoY |
| AUM | INR 1,042 cr (FY26-end) | +37% | Crossed INR 1,000 cr milestone this year |
| Disbursements | INR 443.54 cr (FY26) | +45% | — |
| GNPA / NNPA | 1.77% / 0.65% | improved from 1.84% GNPA last year | — |
| Capital adequacy | 38.62% | — | Comfortable headroom |
| Cost of borrowing | 10.88% (Q4 FY26) | down from 11.07% (Q4 FY25) | Company issued a post-call correction: on the live call a wrong figure (63%→61%) was read out due to audio issue; correct is 10.88% → guided to ~10.70% over next 1-2 yrs |
| Cost-to-income | 63.14% | down from 67.49% | — |
> One-off: management's live verbal answer on cost-of-borrowing trajectory (quoted as "63% to 61%") was a
> mis-statement due to audio issues; a written correction in the transcript clarifies actual cost of borrowing
> is 10.88% (Q4FY26), guided down to ~10.70% over the next 1-2 years. Track the corrected figure only.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- Disbursement growth: targeting ~INR 600 cr disbursements for FY27 (vs INR 443.54 cr in FY26)
- AUM growth: FY27 exit AUM guided at INR 1,300-1,400 cr (optimistic case INR 1,500 cr)
- Medium-term: AUM to cross INR 2,000 cr within 2-3 years (management target INR 2,000-2,500 cr in 2.5-3 years)
- Long-term (3-5 yr+): ambition of INR 10,000-20,000 cr AUM book (no firm timeline — "clarity will come in the next two years")
- Cost of borrowing: guided down from 10.88% (Q4FY26) to ~10.70% over next 1-2 years, aided by the rating upgrade
- ROE: management expects to broadly maintain current ~12-13% level, with some optimism toward ~18% longer term (answer was somewhat inconsistent/unclear on call)
- Capital raise: NHB allows leverage up to 12x but banks cap practical leverage at 5x-6x; once leverage nears that band, company will raise equity — possibly Q4 FY27 if the year progresses well, otherwise Q1/Q2 FY28
- Geographic expansion: 10-15 new branches planned in Tamil Nadu and Telangana by end of this year (FY27); no further expansion planned in existing states (Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, MP)
order book & pipeline: Not applicable (lending business — see AUM/disbursement guidance above).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- Single standalone entity; no subsidiaries.
- Geographic mix: Rajasthan + Gujarat together ~77% of AUM (historically dominant, first-mover states).
- Newer states (Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka) expanded into over the last ~1.5 years and are now the
  fastest-growing regions, ahead of Gujarat/Rajasthan growth rates.
- Planned next-leg expansion: Tamil Nadu and Telangana (research underway; branches to open by year-end FY27).
- Management expects Rajasthan/Gujarat's AUM share to normalize toward parity with other states over 2-3 years
  as newer geographies scale.
growth verticals / optionality:
- Digital/collections technology: "SRG SRAJAN" ERP program with AI-assisted calling under development (no cost
  incurred yet — still in R&D; dedicated IT team being built out).
- Rating upgrade (Acuité A- Stable) has opened three new funding avenues: previously non-lending banks now open
  to financing the company, equity market access improved, and NCD market has strengthened; company draws
  support from 36 lenders/NCD investors including SBI, HDFC Bank, LIC Housing Finance, plus mutual fund
  investment in its NCDs.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- 20-25 years of on-ground underwriting experience in self-employed rural/semi-urban segment where borrowers
  typically lack formal documentation (no GST, ITR, Udyam, Aadhaar-linked banking history) — credit team
  physically visits customer locations (e.g., Kirana store owners) to assess cash flows, purchase patterns and
  vendor relationships in lieu of standard documentation.
- Collection infrastructure: ~97% of EMI collections via banking channel; only ~4-5% cash collection; dedicated
  call-center follow-up team recovers ~90% of the ~14-15% cheque-bounce rate within the same month (0-30 day
  bucket), with ~97% of bounced-cheque amounts recovered within 30 days.
- 36 lenders/NCD investors including marquee names (SBI, HDFC Bank, LIC Housing Finance) plus mutual fund NCD
  participation — signals funding-market trust that is harder for smaller/newer HFCs to replicate.
margins & cost dynamics:
- NIM stable at ~11% (Q4: 11.28%; FY26: 10.91%); management expects this to be the sustainable long-term level
  despite rapid AUM growth.
- Cost of borrowing down to 10.88% (Q4FY26) from 11.07% (Q4FY25), aided by rating upgrade; guided toward ~10.70%
  over next 1-2 years.
- Cost-to-income ratio improved to 63.14% from 67.49% YoY on operating leverage and sales efficiency gains.
- Average ticket size up 41% YoY to INR 15.44 lakh, driven by expansion into newer (higher-cost) markets and
  rising construction costs — not a strategic shift in customer profile, per management.
- Average LTV up from ~46.6% to 50.7% YoY — management attributes this to the nature of the housing-finance
  product evolving with rising property/construction costs, not a deliberate risk-taking strategy.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- 10-15 new branches planned in Tamil Nadu and Telangana within FY27 (research phase currently underway).
- AUM per branch improved to INR 10.86 cr (Q4FY26) from INR 8.44 cr (Q4FY25); AUM per employee improved to
  INR 1.05 cr from INR 0.88 cr — productivity gains to watch as new branches scale (typically dilutive early on).
- Watch: whether the 10-15 branch southern expansion actually completes within FY27 as guided, and how quickly
  new branches reach the INR 25 cr/branch maturity level management targets (against a longer-run per-branch
  target of ~INR 110 cr).
capital allocation:
- Capital adequacy comfortable at 38.62%, well above regulatory requirement.
- Equity raise contemplated once leverage approaches the practical 5x-6x band banks allow (NHB technically
  permits up to 12x) — timing flagged as possibly Q4 FY27, or Q1/Q2 FY28 if this year's growth trajectory
  slips.
- No dividend, buyback, or other capital-return commentary on this call.
risks & watch-items:
- Geographic concentration: Rajasthan + Gujarat still ~77% of AUM; GNPA flagged as proportionately higher in
  Rajasthan simply due to portfolio size there, per management (no specific asset-quality red flag cited).
  Diversification into 5 new states is the stated mitigant but execution risk remains.
  Verify next call: whether the Rajasthan GNPA concentration eases as newer states scale.
- Rising ticket sizes (+41% YoY) and rising LTV (46.6%→50.7%) together increase per-loan risk exposure even
  though management maintains this is not a deliberate strategy shift — worth tracking asset quality trend
  here specifically.
- Macro: management downplayed any impact from the "West Asia crisis" and weak monsoon on its predominantly
  self-employed (75-79%) borrower base, citing diversified small-ticket profiles (kirana, dairy, contractors,
  spare-parts) as insulated from macro shocks — an assertion to sanity-check against actual delinquency trends.
- Cost-of-borrowing guidance was verbally mis-stated live on the call (audio issue) and had to be corrected in
  writing post-call — a minor governance/quality-control flag on call execution, though the written correction
  was prompt and clear.
- ROE guidance in the Q&A was somewhat muddled: CEO first cited ~18% aspiration, then walked it back to
  "same, ~12-13%" when pressed by the analyst — lack of a crisp, consistent ROE target/roadmap.
management quality / tone:
- This was Archis Jain's first earnings call as CEO (appointed 2023, with the company since 2018) — opening
  remarks struck a measured, governance-focused tone ("transparency, accountability, long-term perspective").
  MD Vinod Kumar Jain remains active on the call for detailed financial/strategic answers.
- Overall tone was confident and growth-oriented but answers on ROE trajectory and cost-of-borrowing showed
  some lack of precision/preparation (leading to the on-call audio correction and an inconsistent ROE answer).
- Management was transparent in publishing a written correction for the cost-of-borrowing mis-statement rather
  than leaving the (materially wrong, unfavorable-sounding "63% to 61%") figure uncorrected in the transcript.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Management frames the opportunity as still nascent at an industry level: cites ~4% of India's population
  covered by formal housing loans today, implying large runway from incremental formal-credit penetration.
- Average home construction cost cited as having roughly doubled to tripled in recent years (from INR 10-15
  lakh to INR 30-35 lakh for a similar ~500-1,000 sq ft house) — a structural driver of the ticket-size increase
  across the entire affordable-housing-finance industry, not company-specific.
- Company explicitly benchmarks itself against larger listed peer Aptus (~INR 13,000 cr AUM) as an aspirational
  scale reference, without giving a firm timeline to close that gap beyond the "3-5 year, INR 10,000-20,000 cr"
  long-term ambition.
- Rating upgrade (Acuité A- Stable) is framed as a genuine funding-mix inflection point — the CEO specifically
  called out mutual funds now investing in the company's NCDs as an unusual validation for a company of this
  size, alongside continuing bank and equity support.

  cr and AUM of INR 1,300-1,500 cr; equity raise flagged as likely in FY27 Q4 or FY28 Q1/Q2 depending on
  leverage; expansion into Tamil Nadu/Telangana (10-15 branches) planned within FY27.
- **Q1 FY27 → check:** disbursement run-rate vs INR 600 cr FY27 target; whether Tamil Nadu/Telangana branch

  any equity-raise announcement.
